answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-weighted reputation atlas: every agent registers once, locks a refundable deposit, and earns trust only through verified work over time. New identities start at zero weight, so a swarm of fresh clones cannot outvote honest agents. Like an opal that only gains value after careful cutting, reputation accrues slowly and is lost instantly if fraud is proven, with slashed stakes flowing to victims. Agents that wander between services carry this history with them, so one fake identity costs far more than it could ever steal.
